memory_update.text: KGS and AROC are the cleanest public-market mappings for U.S. natural gas compression as a reliability and throughput chokepoint; both need later-layer checks for leverage, utilization, and cyclicality.
GTLS is a direct LNG/cryogenic equipment mapping and may be more project-backlog sensitive than compression fleet names; include in later LNG infrastructure pass.
MRC is a lower-attention PVF distribution candidate for gas utility, pipeline, LNG, and industrial infrastructure, but exposure purity requires segment-level verification.

Natural Gas Services Group (NGS) surfaced as a sub-$1B compression equipment/rental candidate with strong node relevance; it was not included in the four-name candidate list only due to overlap and candidate limit, but should be revisited in Layer 1C/speculative-shadow screening.

EFXT appears to be a high-priority underfollowed candidate for the oil/gas reliability node due to disclosed gas compression, processing, aftermarket, and data-center power-generation opportunities backed by backlog.

NGS is a small-cap compression-equipment rental and service candidate with large-horsepower/electric-motor-drive exposure; verify utilization, capex discipline, customer contracts, and component lead times.
DNOW is a second-order PVF/valve/supply-chain infrastructure candidate after MRC Global combination; verify gas utility/midstream mix and integration risk before promoting beyond Layer 1.

Natural gas compression and PVF/valve distribution are investable public-market mappings for gas reliability, LNG export, peaking generation, and industrial electrification adjacency without making a direct commodity-price call.
CECO/legacy Thermon should be separately tested in a follow-up pass for natural gas power, emissions/air-quality systems, heat tracing, load-bank/data-center, and process-heating exposure.
AROC should remain in the underfollowed lane for gas reliability because contract compression and aftermarket services may be recurring infrastructure exposure rather than pure drilling beta.
KGS is a high-purity compression-infrastructure candidate; next layer should test distributed-power materiality, contract tenor, and leverage.
POWL is no longer low-attention, but remains relevant because LNG, utility, and data-center power orders connect oil/gas infrastructure to electrification-adjacent equipment.

MRC Global appears relevant as a PVF distributor and hidden MRO/project-gate supplier for oil/gas, utilities, and energy-transition infrastructure, but was not included in the final four candidates due to market-cap verification gaps; investigate in a later pass.

Best Layer 2 falsification tests: fleet utilization for compression names, backlog conversion and customer concentration for Powell, LNG/project slippage risk, and whether gas infrastructure demand is durable reliability demand or merely commodity-cycle capex.

AROC should remain in the oil/gas reliability node as a mid-cap compression and aftermarket supplier; verify whether demand is structurally linked to LNG, transmission, storage, and gas-fired power rather than only upstream activity.

NGS is a small-cap underfollowed compression rental candidate with direct fleet horsepower evidence; keep as a higher-risk discovery-lane name pending utilization, pricing, customer, and large-horsepower mix checks.

MRC is a low-attention PVF/valve/instrumentation distributor candidate; its low-emission valve disclosure creates a methane-compliance angle that should be tested against revenue mix and margin evidence.

For this node, the less obvious investable map is not only LNG exporters or gas producers; it includes compression horsepower, aftermarket service, PVF distribution, low-emission valves, measurement/instrumentation, and project logistics.

Need a follow-up Layer 1C search for public suppliers of gas turbines/reciprocating engines, gensets, emissions monitoring, cryogenic LNG equipment, and methane detection software/hardware; this pass did not fully cover those adjacent chokepoints.

node: Oil/gas reliability, LNG infrastructure, compression, valves, onsite power, and electrification-adjacent equipment
summary: Combined focused Layer 1B searches: Expanded the direct public-company universe for the gas reliability/LNG/compression/PVF node. The strongest underfollowed candidates cluster around natural-gas compression fleets and aftermarket service, LNG cryogenic equipment, and pipe/valve/fitting distribution. This is not a commodity-price call; the research angle is installed-base uptime, project execution, LNG/gas infrastructure buildout, and recurring service tied to reliability needs. Expanded the universe around the gas reliability/LNG/power-support node with one compression reference name and three underfollowed discovery candidates. The strongest directly supported sub-node is natural gas compression and modular gas/power systems: public disclosures from Kodiak, Enerflex, and Natural Gas Services Group all point to tight compression markets, growing natural gas demand, LNG/export/power generation relevance, and fleet/backlog expansion. A second underfollowed sub-node is PVF distribution and valve/supply-chain infrastructure for midstream, gas utility, downstream, and energy-transition customers, represented by DNOW after its MRC Global combination. No trading recommendation is made; this is a Layer 1B research universe expansion only. Expanded the underfollowed lane for the oil/gas reliability and LNG-power infrastructure node. The most relevant public-market map is not pure E&P commodity beta, but installed-base compression, large-horsepower gas infrastructure services, engineered electrical systems for LNG/data-center/utility loads, and PVF distribution gates.
